title: Holdings and conflicts of interest
description: How to interpret holdings disclosures, author interests and potential conflicts in Stocks to Buy Now Research content.
intro: Stocks to Buy Now Research believes readers should understand the financial interests behind investment commentary. Our contributors may invest in the companies and instruments they discuss. Relevant interests should be considered alongside the research, its assumptions and its risks.
sections: Contributor and company interests

Employees and contractors must disclose material positions or beneficial interests relevant to research they contribute. These include long positions, short positions and options. A company position and an individual contributor’s position are separate interests and must be identified as such.
Disclosures alongside research

Relevant interests should be disclosed alongside the article or research item, including when a contributor provides an alternative viewpoint. A disclosure should identify the instrument, the nature of the interest and the date to which it applies. Material compensated relationships connected to the subject should also be identified.
Funds and indirect holdings

Ownership of a mutual fund or ETF is distinct from direct ownership of every security in that fund. The underlying securities are not treated as direct personal holdings unless the contributor controls those investment decisions.
Positions can change

A disclosure reflects the information stated at its date. Holdings and relationships can change, and a historical disclosure is not a live account statement. This page does not provide a live holdings register.
Questions about an interest

For a question about a particular article, position or relationship, contact support@stockstobuynow.ai with the page URL and ticker. Do not send brokerage passwords, account numbers or private identity documents.

title: Personal trading and disclosure policy
description: Personal trading, minimum holding periods and conflict disclosure standards for Stocks to Buy Now Research employees and contributors.
intro: Our personal-trading policy sets standards for investing responsibly while contributing research. Contributors may own investments they discuss, but must disclose relevant interests and keep their personal trading separate from their responsibility to readers.
sections: Who this policy covers

This policy applies to Stocks to Buy Now Research employees and contractors, including contributors who prepare or review investment content. It covers investments held directly or through accounts they control or in which they have a beneficial interest. Family and household accounts are included when the covered person directs or controls their investment decisions or shares a beneficial interest. Covered investments include stocks, short positions, options, ETFs, mutual funds and cryptocurrencies. Fund holdings are considered at the fund level; individual securities held within a fund are not treated as direct personal holdings unless the person controls those investment decisions.
Conflicts of interest

Before contributing research, employees and contractors must identify material financial or commercial interests connected with its subject. Relevant interests must be disclosed alongside the content. Contributors must raise conflicts that could compromise fair analysis before publication.
Minimum holding period

The minimum holding period is 7 days. Covered employees and contractors must hold a position for at least 7 days before closing it. The rule also applies to positions in accounts covered by this policy, including accounts whose investment decisions they direct or control.

We believe contributors can benefit from investing their own money and understanding the decisions investors face. At the same time, personal trading must not take priority over the responsibility to provide thoughtful, balanced research. A minimum holding period is intended to encourage considered investment decisions and discourage rapid trading around published commentary.

The holding period is one part of managing conflicts of interest. It does not replace the requirement to disclose relevant positions or material commercial interests, and it does not make a contributor’s investment suitable for every reader. Research should be assessed on its reasoning, assumptions and risks, rather than on whether its author owns the investment.

This is a personal-trading rule for people covered by our policy, not a recommended holding period for customers or a promise of investment performance. Readers should choose their own time horizons based on their objectives, circumstances and the risks of the instrument. Questions about the policy can be sent to support@stockstobuynow.ai.
Questions and concerns

Questions about this policy or concerns about a potential conflict should be sent to support@stockstobuynow.ai. Include the relevant research URL and enough detail to identify the issue without sharing private account information.

title: Editorial and commercial disclosures
description: Editorial standards, AI-assisted research, corrections and the distinction between research and commercial relationships.
intro: Stocks to Buy Now Research publishes investment research, educational content and market tools. These standards distinguish our analysis from advertising, commercial relationships and promotion of our own services.
sections: Editorial independence

Research must reflect the author’s analysis and the evidence available. Advertisers, sponsors and commercial partners must not determine research conclusions or present paid placement as independent editorial judgement. A business relationship does not by itself establish an investment case.
Authors, sources and review

Public articles should identify their author, distinguish analysis from reported facts and identify supporting sources. The public-article workflow requires an identified reviewer and an explicit publication decision. Substantive corrections and revisions should be distinguished from routine data refreshes.
AI-assisted research

AI tools may support research, drafting and data analysis. Their use does not remove the responsibility to check factual claims, assumptions and calculations. Material AI assistance should be disclosed where relevant to the content.
Our subscriptions and app

We promote our own Stocks to Buy Now Research subscriptions, app features and educational tools. These placements are offers for our services. A subscription purchase does not establish the accuracy of a forecast or guarantee an investment outcome.
Advertising and compensated relationships

Paid placements and sponsored content must be clearly identified. Where a referral or affiliate link may earn compensation, that relationship must be disclosed near the relevant offer. Material business relationships connected with an article’s subject must also be disclosed. These standards do not imply that every type of commercial arrangement described here is currently offered.
Corrections and questions

To report a possible error or ask about a commercial relationship, email support@stockstobuynow.ai with the page URL, the claim in question and any supporting information. Material corrections should be explained on the affected article.

title: Investment return calculations and performance disclosures
description: How stock research results, SPY comparisons, option-price moves and forecast illustrations are calculated and what they do not measure.
intro: A price move, a weighted research average and a portfolio return measure different things. This page explains the methods used in our scorecard, benchmark comparisons, options examples and prediction tools.
sections: Stock research entry and exit prices

The current target-date scorecard uses the first eligible exchange open after the later of publication and recommendation timestamps. It exits at the saved target-date close, or the next session if that date is closed. Prices are model inputs from daily adjusted market data.
Dividends, splits and gross returns

The scorecard metadata describes its prices as split- and dividend-adjusted. Those adjustments are reflected in the model prices; this should not be described as a separate cash-dividend ledger. Gross signal returns do not represent an investor’s result after all trading costs, subscription charges and taxes.
Benchmark comparisons

The US stock comparison uses SPY over matching entry and exit dates and matching weights. The scorecard’s European listings are measured in their listing currencies and excluded from the US benchmark comparison. SPY is an exchange-traded fund used as the benchmark proxy, not a brokerage account identical to a reader’s.
Estimated costs

The displayed estimated-net scenarios subtract 0.10 or 0.20 percentage points of entry notional as assumed round-trip friction. These are illustrations, not measured brokerage expenses, and they do not establish a reader’s after-tax or after-subscription return.
Annualisation is not a realised yearly return

The scorecard annualises its weighted gross return using ((1 + return ÷ 100)^(365 ÷ weighted-average holding days) − 1) × 100. This extrapolates a holding-period average to one year. It does not show that a portfolio earned that annual rate or that the same opportunities could be repeatedly reinvested.
Separate portfolio simulations

The downloadable calculation metadata also describes a retrospective contribution model. It uses regular contributions, normalised entry allocations and specific cash rules; sale proceeds are not reinvested and cash earns no interest. Its time-weighted return, gain on contributions and drawdown are different measures from the weighted signal average. Read the model assumptions before comparing these figures.
Options results

Option result cards compare a recorded premium with the previous session’s close, using (comparison premium ÷ previous premium − 1) × 100. One-contract illustrations multiply the per-share premium change by 100 for a standard contract. Adjusted contracts can use different multipliers. The figures are before costs and are price comparisons, not proof that a customer or publisher executed those trades.
Predictions and hypothetical paths

Prediction charts illustrate assumptions and possible paths. They are not realised investment results. Simulated seasonality and event swings do not establish that the forecast or the illustrated timing will occur. Historical outcomes do not guarantee future returns.
Checking a calculation

Use the scorecard, calculation metadata and downloadable ledger to inspect entries, exits, weights and benchmark windows. For a correction, send the page URL or signal identifier and the specific calculation you believe is wrong to support@stockstobuynow.ai.

title: Research disclaimer and service information
description: The scope and limitations of Stocks to Buy Now Research information, forecasts, market data and educational tools.
intro: Stocks to Buy Now Research provides investment research, educational content and tools. Read this information alongside our Privacy Policy & Terms of Use and the terms shown when purchasing a subscription.
sections: Research and education

General research, lessons and example portfolios do not by themselves assess your complete financial circumstances, objectives or ability to bear losses. A stock or options idea is not a promise that it is suitable for every reader.
Investment risks

Investments can lose value. Options can lose their entire premium, while some short or leveraged positions can expose an investor to losses beyond the initial cash committed. Examples do not account for every person’s fees, taxes, borrowing conditions or execution constraints.
Data, forecasts and availability

Market data can be delayed, incomplete or revised. Forecasts depend on assumptions and may be wrong. Data refresh frequency and comparison dates vary by feature; a daily dataset should not be interpreted as a continuously updating executable quote.
Accounts, subscriptions and privacy

The existing Privacy Policy & Terms of Use describes account information, service providers, subscriptions, cancellation and refund arrangements. Review the relevant checkout and payment-provider information for your purchase. This disclosure does not change existing rights or billing terms.
Responsibility and corrections

Check material information before acting and consider professional advice appropriate to your circumstances. Report suspected errors to support@stockstobuynow.ai with the affected page URL and supporting evidence. Nothing on this page removes rights that cannot lawfully be excluded.
